newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-AGASSI RALLIES TO CLINCH FOR U.S. OVER NETHERLANDS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-AGASSI RALLIES TO CLINCH FOR U.S. OVER NETHERLANDS.

text.p: The United States took an insurmountable 3-1 lead over the Netherlands in their Davis Cup quarter-final when Andre Agassi roared back from a two-sets deficit to beat Jan Siemerink 3-6 3-6 6-3 6-3 6-4 Sunday.
Agassi's 15th successive Cup victory set up a September 19-21 semifinal clash against Australia in world group play.

Siemerink's big lefthanded serve-and-volley style and lone breaks in the first two sets put him ahead but, as in his collapse against Jim Courier on Friday, the Dutchman could not hold on, while Agassi's baseline game awakened.
The American took the third set with a key service break in the opening game. He built it to 5-3 before breaking again in the final game after Siemerink saved three set points.
The momentum clearly shifted to Agassi at that point, and the American crowd voiced their delight.
Agassi claimed the fourth set with a lone service break in the second game as Siemerink helplessly watched a topspin-lob winner spin in.
In the deciding fifth set, Agassi broke in the opening game as the Dutchman double-faulted at break point. The American held for 5-3.

Agassi had three match points at 0-40 before Siemerink erased two with volley winners. But Agassi hit a searing cross-court backhand service return winner to complete the stirring come-from-behind win.
